indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the `_transition_hints` JQL to the probed project (`project = <key> AND issuetype = ...`) and thread `project_key` through `_transition_hints`.
evidence: `jql = f'issuetype = "{issue_type}" ORDER BY created DESC'` (mapping_probe.py:240) has no project filter
`_transition_hints(port, issue_types)` receives no project_key (build_mapping_layer passes only issue_types)
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:91: `return f'project = {_validate_project_key(project)} AND statusCategory != "Done"'` — the established project-scoping convention
Docstring claims hints are 'for one sample issue per discovered type' of THIS project, but the query is instance-wide
indeterminate.finding: `_transition_hints` builds JQL `issuetype = "{issue_type}" ORDER BY created DESC` with NO `project = <key>` clause, so for a per-project probe it samples issues (and their transitions) from ANY project the credential can see, not the project being probed. Every other JQL in the codebase scopes by project (e.g. fetcher.py:91, _links.py:39, _hierarchy.py:75).
indeterminate.suggested_fix: Pass `project_key` into `_transition_hints` and build `jql = f'project = {project_key} AND issuetype = "{issue_type}" ORDER BY created DESC'` (mirroring fetcher's project-scoped queries).

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'probe ran and project is empty' from 'probe reached nothing': if all core getters return empty, emit a non-zero exit / explicit warning rather than a silently-empty block.
evidence: `_soft` returns `default` on `except Exception` for every getter (mapping_probe.py:64-69)
`build_mapping_layer` assembles issue_types/statuses/... with no liveness check; empty axes just produce empty identity maps and `_notes`
The top-level handler only catches exceptions from build_probe/build_mapping_layer themselves (which never propagate from the soft getters), so a wholly-failed probe still returns 0
The `_honesty_notes` cover Cloud-only hierarchy and partial transitions but never signal 'the probe reached no data at all'
indeterminate.finding: The probe is fail-open: every port getter swallows all exceptions via `_soft` and returns an empty default, and `build_mapping_layer` never asserts that any getter actually returned data. An auth failure (403), an unreachable instance, or a valid-but-nonexistent context therefore yields an empty-but-well-formed mapping block emitted with exit 0 — indistinguishable from a project that genuinely has empty vocabulary.
indeterminate.suggested_fix: After gathering, if issue_types and statuses (and priorities/link_types) are all empty, treat it as a probe failure — write an explicit warning and return non-zero — instead of emitting an empty suggestion at exit 0.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test injecting a raising jira client into _JiraProbePort to assert each getter degrades to an empty result rather than crashing.
evidence: mapping_probe.py _soft: 'try: return fn() except Exception: return default'
Module docstring: 'Fail-soft on EVERY external getter — a Jira instance that 403s or omits an attribute yields an empty axis + an honest note, never a fabricated value or a crash.'
test_probe.py _FakePort getters unconditionally return canned lists (e.g. issue_types returns [dict(t) for t in _ISSUE_TYPES]); no getter raises, so no degraded path is driven.
ABSENCE: no test injects a raising client into _JiraProbePort or asserts an empty axis + _notes on a getter failure.
indeterminate.finding: The fail-soft degradation contract of _JiraProbePort._soft — the module's central design claim that 'a Jira instance that 403s or omits an attribute yields an empty axis + an honest note, never a fabricated value or a crash' — has no test. _FakePort always returns canned data and never raises, so the try/except in _soft and the empty-axis fallback are never exercised.
scenarios: A real Jira 403s on statuses() and the fail-soft wrapper silently changes behavior (e.g. re-raises after a refactor) — no test would catch the regression.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with issue types lacking hierarchyLevel asserting the 'hierarchy' key is absent and the 'hierarchy omitted' honesty note is emitted.
evidence: mapping_probe.py: 'if hierarchy: layer["hierarchy"] = hierarchy' and _honesty_notes appends 'hierarchy omitted: no issue type reported a hierarchyLevel (Data Center / older Jira).'
test_probe.py _ISSUE_TYPES: every entry has a hierarchyLevel key ({'name':'Epic',...,'hierarchyLevel':1}, etc.)
ABSENCE: no test supplies issue types WITHOUT hierarchyLevel to assert 'hierarchy' is absent and the omission note is emitted (the explicit Data Center scenario).
indeterminate.finding: The hierarchy-omission path — a headline design-of-record behavior ('hierarchyLevel is Cloud-only: when absent, hierarchy is dropped rather than invented', plus the _honesty_notes 'hierarchy omitted' footnote) — is never tested. The only issue-type fixture (_ISSUE_TYPES) supplies hierarchyLevel on every type, so _hierarchy() returning empty and the caller dropping 'hierarchy' + emitting the note is uncovered.
scenarios: On Data Center (no hierarchyLevel), a regression that fabricates ranks or omits the honesty note would pass CI.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test monkeypatching build_probe (or build_mapping_layer) to raise, asserting exit code 1 and the actionable stderr message.
evidence: _cli/__init__.py: 'except Exception as exc: sys.stderr.write(f"Error: could not probe Jira project {key!r}: {exc}\n" ...); return 1'
test_probe.py: all three CLI-driving tests install a happy _FakePort via _install_fake_port and assert code == 0; none monkeypatch build_probe to raise.
ABSENCE: no test asserts the exit-1 UX-error path when the probe fails.
indeterminate.finding: The CLI probe-failure error path is untested: _bridge_suggest_mapping wraps build_probe/build_mapping_layer in try/except and returns exit code 1 with a specific stderr message on any failure. No test drives a failing build_probe or build_mapping_layer to assert the exit code and error text.
scenarios: A refactor swallows the exception or returns 0 on failure, or drops the actionable JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_PAT hint — no test catches it.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that _emit_nested_toml/_emit_config_toml raises ConfigError on an unsupported scalar value type in the mapping block.
evidence: _config_writer.py _render_scalar: 'raise ConfigError(f"cannot serialize config value of type {type(value).__name__!r} ...")'
Docstring for _emit_nested_toml: 'Reuses _render_value so ... the fail-closed guard on an unsupported scalar type match _emit_toml.'

test_probe.py test_emit_toml_still_fail_closed_on_nesting only exercises cw._emit_toml, not _emit_nested_toml/_emit_config_toml with an unsupported scalar (e.g. a dict-valued leaf that isn't a table, or a None/set value).
indeterminate.finding: The new _render_scalar fail-closed guard (raising ConfigError on an unsupported value type) reached through the NEW _emit_nested_toml / _emit_config_toml path is untested. The only fail-closed regression test targets the UNTOUCHED _emit_toml, not the new nested emitter that must enforce the same contract on the mapping block.
scenarios: A probe axis value of an unsupported type flows into the mapping block; a regression that silently emits garbage TOML instead of raising ConfigError would pass.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Escape/quote issue-type names before interpolating them into the JQL string in `_transition_hints` (mapping_probe.py:240).
evidence: `jql = f'issuetype = "{issue_type}" ORDER BY created DESC'` (mapping_probe.py:240)

`issue_type` originates from `port.issue_types()` -> `raw_types`/`issue_types` in build_mapping_layer, i.e. Jira-server-supplied `name` values normalized via `_attr(t, "name", "")` (mapping_probe.py issue_types / build_mapping_layer)
No escaping/quoting of the interpolated `issue_type` before it reaches `port.search_issues(jql)` (mapping_probe.py:241)
indeterminate.finding: Jira-server-supplied issue-type names are interpolated into a JQL query string with only surrounding double-quotes and no escaping, so a name containing a double-quote (or JQL metacharacters) breaks out of the quoted literal — an untrusted-external-input-to-query-sink taint flow.
scenarios: A Jira project defines an issue type whose name contains a double-quote or JQL operators; the constructed JQL is malformed or its predicate is altered when sent to search_issues.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Escape control characters (newline, tab, etc.) in `_render_scalar` and `_toml_key`, or reject names containing them, before writing them into rebar.toml (_config_writer.py:102,~123).
evidence: `s = value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')` — only `\` and `"` escaped (_config_writer.py:102)
`_toml_key` applies the same two-replacement escaping to keys (_config_writer.py ~123)

Jira status/type/link/field names flow verbatim into `status_map`/`type_map`/`create_defaults` keys and values in build_mapping_layer, then through `_emit_config_toml`/`_emit_nested_toml` -> `_render_value`/`_toml_key` into the written file
`_suggest_mapping_write` writes the emitted text to `rebar.toml` via atomic replace (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py `_suggest_mapping_write`)
indeterminate.finding: The TOML emitters `_render_scalar` and `_toml_key` escape only backslash and double-quote — not newlines or other control characters — so Jira-server-supplied vocabulary names/values written to `rebar.toml` on `--write` can inject raw newlines and additional attacker-influenced TOML lines (taint flow: external API data -> config-file sink).
scenarios: A Jira instance exposes a status/issue-type/field name containing a newline; `--write` emits it inside a TOML basic string producing invalid TOML or injecting an extra `key = "value"` line into the operator's rebar.toml.
indeterminate.suggested_fix: In `_render_scalar`/`_toml_key`, additionally escape TOML basic-string control chars (\n, \r, \t, and other C0 controls) per the TOML spec, or raise ConfigError on a name containing a raw control character (fail-closed).
